assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamical mean-field theory, built on the infinite-dimension limit, gave condensed-matter theory its first controlled, non-perturbative route to Mott physics and strongly correlated metals. Combined with electronic-structure methods (DFT+DMFT) it is now a standard tool for predicting and interpreting spectra and phase stability of real correlated materials. Originality, clarity and lasting reach are all high.
assessment.attribution: The decisive steps are the infinite-dimension limit of the Hubbard model (Metzner and Vollhardt), the mapping onto a self-consistent impurity problem (Georges and Kotliar) and the Mott-transition solution. The supplied credit names capture much of this, but Metzner is not among the credited names and I cannot propose him. Within the supplied names I would favour Georges, Kotliar and Vollhardt as a defensible trio.
assessment.maturity: More than thirty years of use, many independent implementations and quantitative agreement with photoemission and optical spectra in several materials families. Recognition is, if anything, overdue.
uncertainties: Credit for the original infinite-dimension formulation is not fully represented by the supplied names.
Quantitative predictive power depends on the impurity solver and double-counting choices, and is uneven across materials.
Whether the committee regards this as a method or a discovery is a judgement call.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Room-temperature tunnel magnetoresistance in magnetic tunnel junctions, and the later large TMR in crystalline MgO barriers, turned spin-dependent tunnelling into a technology: read heads, MRAM and spin-transfer devices. The physics (spin-polarised tunnelling, coherent symmetry filtering through MgO, first predicted by band-structure calculations) is a clear and widely appreciated example of electronic-structure theory meeting experiment.
assessment.attribution: Miyazaki and Moodera independently reported reproducible room-temperature TMR in 1995. Parkin's group and Yuasa's group reported giant TMR in MgO in 2004, following the theoretical prediction of Butler and of Mathon and Umerski (not credited here). A prize cannot cover all four credited names, and the choice between the Miyazaki/Moodera discovery and the MgO engineering step is a genuine allocation problem. I would propose Miyazaki, Moodera and Parkin, leaving Yuasa and the theorists out only for space.
assessment.maturity: Three decades of confirmation and large commercial deployment. Fully mature. It follows the 2007 prize for GMR, which may reduce its perceived novelty.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2007 GMR prize may weigh against it.
The theoretical predictors of MgO coherent tunnelling are not in the credited names.
Yuasa's equal claim on the MgO step is left out of the proposed trio.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Topological insulators and the quantum spin Hall effect established that band structure carries a topological invariant, with protected edge and surface states and a Z2 classification that now reaches across materials. Strong spin-orbit coupling and band inversion are exactly the ingredients first-principles calculations handle well, so the field is also a showcase for predictive materials theory.
assessment.attribution: The theoretical foundation is Kane and Mele (Z2 invariant, spin Hall insulator in graphene), with Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposing HgTe and Molenkamp's group observing the quantum spin Hall state in 2007. Hasan's group observed the 3D phase in Bi-Sb and Bi2Se3. Kane, Mele and Molenkamp is a coherent trio for the quantum spin Hall step, but 3D topological insulators and Hasan, Moore, Balents and others are left outside it. B008 and B011 overlap strongly with this entry and I would not rank them separately.
assessment.maturity: Strong independent confirmation over about twenty years, with a durable conceptual framework. Mature. Direct technological payoff is still limited.
uncertainties: The allocation across 2D versus 3D topological insulators and across theory versus experiment is disputed and a three-person limit forces an unresolved choice.
Bernevig and Zhang are not among the credited names.
Overlap with B008 and B011 means a prize here would absorb much of those proposals.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene opened a tunable platform where flat bands produce correlated insulators and superconductivity, and it prompted a broad moiré materials field. The prediction of flat bands at a magic angle from continuum-model band-structure arguments, followed by experimental realisation, is an unusually clean theory-to-experiment story. It also connects directly to the stability and properties of two-dimensional materials.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the 2011 theoretical prediction; Jarillo-Herrero's group made the 2018 observation of correlated insulators and superconductivity. Andrei's group contributed early STM evidence of flat bands and twist-angle physics. The theory plus first-experiment configuration is clear, but Andrei's claim, and that of others in the 2018 flurry, are a source of dispute.
assessment.maturity: Replicated widely since 2018, though the nature of the superconductivity and correlated states is still debated. Reasonably early for recognition.
uncertainties: The microscopic origin of superconductivity is unresolved.
Sample inhomogeneity and twist-angle disorder complicate interpretation.
Andrei's contribution is not covered by a three-person split.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices realise Hubbard-type models with tunable parameters, giving a clean testing ground for correlated-matter theory, including the superfluid-Mott transition and later quantum-gas microscopy. As someone who works on model Hamiltonians for real solids, I value the quantum-simulator idea as a complement to numerical approaches, though its quantitative reach for hard problems such as the 2D Hubbard model is still being established.
assessment.attribution: Jaksch, Zoller and collaborators proposed the Bose-Hubbard realisation; Greiner and Bloch observed the Mott transition; Esslinger realised fermionic Mott states; Bloch and Greiner developed the microscope. The five credited names cannot all be recognised, and the ordering of theory versus experiment is open. I would propose Bloch, Cirac and Zoller; Jaksch is not credited, and Greiner and Esslinger remain strong alternatives.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed and highly cited across many groups. Recognition would not be premature, although the 2012 and 2022 AMO prizes cover related ground.
uncertainties: Overlap with earlier AMO prizes and with B016, B030 and B007.
Allocation among at least five strong contributors is not resolved.
The quantum-simulation payoff for real materials remains partly prospective.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Altermagnetism identifies a third class of collinear magnetic order with compensated moments and spin-split bands, produced by crystal symmetry rather than net magnetisation. This falls squarely in my own area of magnetism and calls for the kind of symmetry-based, first-principles analysis I work with. It has potential for spintronics with no stray field and fast dynamics.
assessment.attribution: The conceptual classification and symmetry framework were developed by Šmejkal, Sinova and Jungwirth, with parallel work by Hayami, Yanase and others and earlier related work on spin-split antiferromagnets. The supplied trio is plausible but earlier and parallel work may complicate the claim.
assessment.maturity: Spin-split bands have been seen in MnTe and CrSb by ARPES since 2024, but the field is only a few years old and many device claims are untested. This is likely premature for a prize now.
uncertainties: Premature: independent confirmation is recent and technological consequences are not shown.
Priority relative to Hayami, Yanase and earlier spin-group work is not settled.
I have a professional interest in the topic and should be cautious about being too favourable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Aharonov-Bohm effect and Berry's geometric phase show that gauge potentials and parameter-space geometry have physical consequences. Berry curvature underlies the anomalous Hall effect, polarisation theory and topological band theory, so the concept pervades modern electronic-structure and condensed-matter physics. Originality and depth are very high.
assessment.attribution: Aharonov and Bohm (1959) and Berry (1984) are distinct discoveries; Bohm died in 1992 and cannot be recognised, and Pancharatnam and Ehrenberg-Siday are important precursors. Aharonov and Berry is a workable pair, though joining two separate discoveries is conceptually loose.
assessment.maturity: The Aharonov-Bohm effect has been confirmed in many experiments and Berry phases are routinely measured. Recognition is well overdue, but the entry is closer to concept than to a single decisive experiment.
uncertainties: Bohm is deceased, which complicates the claim for the Aharonov-Bohm effect.
Joining two separate discoveries in one prize is awkward.
The Nobel emphasis on experimentally established discovery may disfavour a conceptual entry.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Spin ice, with its residual entropy and its excitations that behave as emergent magnetic monopoles, is a clean case of emergent gauge structure in a frustrated magnet. It relates directly to my interest in magnetic materials and spin models, and the Coulomb-phase picture is conceptually elegant.
assessment.attribution: Harris, Bramwell and Gingras, Castelnovo, Moessner and Sondhi, Fennell and Morris and others each made decisive contributions to the discovery and the monopole picture. The credited names cannot cover all of these, so a three-person configuration is unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Neutron scattering and thermodynamic evidence is considerable, but the monopole interpretation is still contested in detail, and impact beyond frustrated magnetism is limited.
uncertainties: Experimental monopole signatures are debated.
Attribution is spread across more than three contributors.
Wider impact beyond a specialised family of materials is limited so far.
